Multi-Donor Trust Fund for Justice Sector Support

description.narrative: Overall objective is to facilitate Serbia’s justice sector EU integration, establish a justice sector performance framework and strengthen aid coordination in Serbia’s justice sector, by providing focused short-term support to the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) to strengthen its capacity and complete key judicial modernization analyses and actions. It supports three key development challenges for Serbia’s justice sector: strengthening judicial and prosecutorial independence, accountability and efficiency. Outcome objective 1: Improved access to justice in Serbia through more concentrated, transparent and effective legal aid programmes available to all citizens, including women, minorities and vulnerable groups in all regions. Outcome objective 2: Decisions on ICT investments in the Serbian judiciary are made strategically to maximise the effectiveness and efficiency gains and reduce the overall investment costs.
Projektet syftar till att slutföra en insats för införande av rättshjälp i Serbien, kombinerat med ökad biståndseffektivitet genom stöd via en fond där sex andra givare bidrar

Sida will join the WB multi-donor TF fund to support Serbia's justice sector EU integration and strengthen aid coordination in the sector. This project is a continuation of previous free legal aid project that was implemented through UNDP. The main focus is on improving access to justice in Serbia through more concentrated, transparent and effective legal aid programmes available to all citizens.

During the reporting period, the main focus in the sector was on aligning the judicial and prosecutorial legislation with the constitutional changes that were adopted in 2022. Intense legislative activity was necessary to ensure the effective operations of the restructured High Judicial Council (HJC) and High Prosecutorial Council (HPC), introduce a new automated case management system, and implement a Human Resources Management strategy in the justice system.
Overall, during the reporting period, Serbia has made steady progress in some areas of the justice sector reform, such as improved efficiency of the courts, including the reduction of backlogs and the introduction of more streamlined judicial procedures, improvement in the quality of court services, enhanced institutional capacities, more use of evidence-based strategy and decision-making in the justice sector, and improved access to justice. This is the so-called first generation of reforms, which focused to a large extent on facilitating key legislative changes and laying the necessary foundations for a strong judicial system. After the adoption of changes in the Constitution, new mechanisms for the election of judicial and prosecutorial office holders need to be installed in order to remove the executive from the immediate selection process. The Venice Commission has also highlighted in its opinion that the legislative amendments should be accompanied by a change in legal culture within the judiciary, to ensure the promotion of independence of the judiciary and autonomy of the prosecution in practice.
The MDTF continued to support this ambitious legislative initiative by providing technical assistance to develop the set of judicial and prosecutorial laws and the consultation process around them and strengthening the institutional capacities in the justice sector. The Embassy has participated in several events related to this process, sometimes with high level engagement, with the Ambassador delivering keynote speeches.
The main outputs under the World Bank-executed part of the Trust Fund during 2023 were as follows:
- Dissemination of 2021 Serbia Judicial Functional Review. An Action Plan with activities supporting the key stakeholders, including the Supreme Public Prosecutor's Office (SPPO), HJC, HPC, the Supreme Court (SC), and the MoJ has been developed to assist the implementation of the Functional Review.
The Functional Review is the flagship report of the MDTF and a central analytical piece, providing an all-encompassing inventory of sector performance and remaining challenges in relation to EU standards. The Functional Review reflects the changes that the justice system has undergone, identifies new areas and priorities for reform and outlines key recommendations, thus providing a roadmap of what needs to be done to bring Serbia's justice system in line with EU standards. It represents an objective analysis of current sector performance and measures progress against the 2014 Judicial Functional Review baseline and the 2019 Functional Review of the Prosecution System,
- Continued support to the SPPO and the MoJ to improve their institutional capacity for monitoring and reporting on the EU accession process,
- Completing and disseminating the Guide for the Self-Representation of MSMEs. The aim of the Guide is to improve the legal literacy of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises by making them familiar with legal proceedings and giving them answers to the questions they may have before addressing the court regarding misdemeanors and economic offenses,
- Support to judicial authorities to investigate, prosecute, and try high-level corruption cases in an impartial and transparent manner through the finalization of the analysis of processing of corruption cases,
- Continued support to the SPPO in processing anti-money laundering cases and cases involving digital property and improving its institutional capacity for monitoring and reporting on the EU accession process,
- Following the request by the MoJ to support the strengthening of commercial justice, the MDTF team has conducted the Commercial Courts Needs Assessment to identify the challenges in the system and issue recommendations,
- A Human Resource Analysis of the HJC and its Administrative Office has been conducted. The analysis identifies the human resource needs in line with the new legislative framework and newly introduced competencies of the HJC, proposes the new organizational structure, and makes recommendations for enhancing the human resource capacities of the Administrative Office and strengthening Human Resource Management in HJC. The results of the Human Resource Analysis were presented at the end of December 2023,
- The outlines for two brochures (a Brochure on Ethics for judges and a Brochure on Disciplinary liability and procedure) have been drafted. Both outlines were agreed with the HJC. The final brochures will be produced in 2024.
These activities are expected to have a cumulative impact on the main goal of the MDTF, which is improved independence, transparency, and access to the justice in Serbia.
